title: Chinese Cinderella
author: Adeline Yen Mah
blurb: A neglected daughter finally wins her father’s approval through success at school in 1950s Hong Kong.
source: A neglected daughter wins her father's approval through academic success
heading: From Chinese Cinderella - Adeline Yen Mah
context: Growing up in a wealthy family in 1950s Hong Kong, Mah should have had an enviable childhood, but she was rejected by her dominating stepmother and despised by her brothers and sisters. She was sent to a boarding school and left there. In this extract from her autobiography she relates one of the few occasions when she went home.

paragraphs.html: Time went by relentlessly and it was Saturday again. Eight weeks more and it would be the end of term ... in my case perhaps the end of school forever.

Four of us were playing Monopoly. My heart was not in it and I was losing steadily. Outside it was hot and there was a warm wind blowing. The radio warned of a possible typhoon the next day. It was my turn and I threw the dice. As I played, the thought of leaving school throbbed at the back of my mind like a persistent toothache.
'Adeline!' Ma-mien Valentino was calling.
'You can't go now,' Mary protested. 'For once I'm winning. One, two, three, four. Good! You've landed on my property. Thirty-five dollars, please. Oh, good afternoon, Mother Valentino!'
We all stood up and greeted her.
'Adeline, didn't you hear me call you? Hurry up downstairs! Your chauffeur is waiting to take you home!'
Full of foreboding, I ran downstairs as in a nightmare, wondering who had died this time. Father's chauffeur assured me everyone was healthy.
'Then why are you taking me home?' I asked.
'How should I know?' he answered defensively, shrugging his shoulders. 'Your guess is as good as mine. They give the orders and I carry them out.'
During the short drive home, my heart was full of dread and I wondered what I had done wrong. Our car stopped at an elegant villa at mid-level, halfway up the hill between the peak and the harbour.
'Where are we?' I asked foolishly.
'Don't you know anything?' the chauffeur replied rudely. 'This is your new home. Your parents moved here a few months ago.'
'I had forgotten,' I said as I got out.
Ah Gum opened the door. Inside, it was quiet and cool.
'Where is everyone?'
'Your mother is out playing bridge. Your two brothers and Little Sister are sunbathing by the swimming-pool. Your father is in his room and wants to see you as soon as you get home.'
'See me in his room?' I was overwhelmed by the thought that I had been summoned by Father to enter the Holy of Holies — a place to which I had never been invited. Why? ...

Timidly, I knocked on the door. Father was alone, looking relaxed in his slippers and bathrobe, reading a newspaper. He smiled as I entered and I saw he was in a happy mood. I breathed a small sigh of relief at first but became uneasy again when I wondered why he was being so nice, thinking, Is this a giant ruse on his part to trick me? Dare I let my guard down?
'Sit down! Sit down!' He pointed to a chair. 'Don't look so scared. Here, take a look at this! They're writing about someone we both know, I think.'
He handed me the day's newspaper and there, in one corner, I saw my name ADELINE YEN in capital letters prominently displayed.

'It was announced today that 14-year-old Hong Kong schoolgirl ADELINE JUN-LING YEN of Sacred Heart Canossian School, Caine Road, Hong Kong, has won first prize in the International Play-writing Competition held in London, England, for the 1951—1952 school year. It is the first time that any local Chinese student from Hong Kong has won such a prestigious event. Besides a medal, the prize comes with a cash reward of FIFTY ENGLISH POUNDS. Our sincere congratulations, ADELINE YEN, for bringing honour to Hong Kong. We are proud of you'.
Is it possible? Am I dreaming? Me, the winner?

'I was going up the lift this morning with my friend C.Y. Tung when he showed me this article and asked me, "Is the winner Adeline Jun-ling Yen related to you? The two of you have the same uncommon last name." Now C.Y. himself has a few children about your age but so far none of them has won an international literary prize, as far as I know. So I was quite pleased to tell him you are my daughter. Well done!'

He looked radiant. For once, he was proud of me. In front of his revered colleague, C.Y. Tung, a prominent fellow businessman also from Shanghai, I had given him face. I thought, Is this the big moment I have been waiting for? My whole being vibrated with all the joy in the world. I only had to stretch out my hand to reach the stars.
'Tell me, how did you do it?' he continued. 'How come you won?'

'Well, the rules and regulations were so very complicated. One really has to be dedicated just to understand what they want. Perhaps I was the only one determined enough to enter and there were no other competitors!'
He laughed approvingly. 'I doubt it very much but that's a good answer.'
'Please, Father,' I asked boldly, thinking it was now or never. 'May I go to university in England too, just like my brothers?'
'I do believe you have potential. Tell me, what would you study?'

My heart gave a giant lurch as it dawned on me that he was agreeing to let me go. How marvellous it was simply to be alive! Study? I thought. Going to England is like entering heaven. Does it matter what you do after you get to heaven?
But Father was expecting an answer. What about creative writing? After all, I had just won first prize in an international writing competition!
'I plan to study literature. I'll be a writer.'

'Writer!' he scoffed. 'You are going to starve! What language are you going to write in and who is going to read your writing? Though you may think you're an expert in both Chinese and English, your Chinese is actually rather elementary. As for your English, don't you think the native English speakers can write better than you?'
I waited in silence. I did not wish to contradict him.

'You will go to England with Third Brother this summer and you will go to medical school. After you graduate, you will specialise in obstetrics. Women will always be having babies. Women patients prefer women doctors. You will learn to deliver their babies. That's a foolproof profession for you. Don't you agree?'

Agree? Of course I agreed. Apparently, he had it all planned out. As long as he let me go to university in England, I would study anything he wished. How did that line go in Wordsworth's poem? Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive.
'Father, I shall go to medical school in England and become a doctor. Thank you very, very much.'

relentlessly.what: Time as merciless force that won't stop.
relentlessly.effect: Creates sense of inevitability and doom approaching.

perhaps-forever.quote: perhaps the end of school forever
perhaps-forever.effect: Shows how precarious her position is - education could be snatched away.

heart-not.quote: My heart was not in it

throbbed-toothache.quote: throbbed at the back of my mind like a persistent toothache
throbbed-toothache.effect: Makes abstract anxiety tangible and inescapable.

chauffeur-waiting.quote: Your chauffeur is waiting to take you home!
chauffeur-waiting.effect: Creates immediate tension - being called home is never good.

full-foreboding.what: Expecting the worst before knowing anything.
full-foreboding.effect: Shows learned response - home means danger.

as-nightmare.what: Reality feels unreal in its horror.
as-nightmare.effect: Dissociation from trauma - too terrible to be real.

who-died.effect: Reveals pattern of tragedy in her life.

your-guess.quote: Your guess is as good as mine. They give the orders and I carry them out
your-guess.effect: Even servants don't know - shows her isolation.

heart-dread.quote: my heart was full of dread
heart-dread.what: Heart as container filled with fear.
heart-dread.effect: Makes emotional state physical and overwhelming.

dont-know-anything.effect: Shows her low status - servants can insult her.

i-forgotten.what: Forgotten because never told about move.
i-forgotten.effect: Shows how excluded from family information she is.

father-room.quote: Your father is in his room and wants to see you as soon as you get home
father-room.what: Immediate summons to father's private space.

holy-holies.what: References Jewish temple's most sacred room.
holy-holies.effect: Father's room as forbidden sacred space - he is god-like.

happy-mood.what: Father's happiness is noteworthy and suspicious.
happy-mood.effect: So rare it's frightening - what does it mean?

small-sigh.what: 'Small' shows she doesn't trust the relief.
small-sigh.effect: Years of abuse make her suspicious of kindness.

giant-ruse.quote: Is this a giant ruse on his part to trick me? Dare I let my guard down?
giant-ruse.effect: Abuse victim's mindset - kindness might be trap.

dont-scared.effect: She can't hide her fear even when he's kind.

adeline-capitals.quote: ADELINE YEN in capital letters prominently displayed
adeline-capitals.what: Capitals make her name jump out.
adeline-capitals.effect: First time her name has importance.

prestigious-event.effect: Achievement that matters to father's circle.

bringing-honour.effect: Shows Chinese concept of reflected glory.

is-possible.quote: Is it possible? Am I dreaming? Me, the winner?
is-possible.effect: Cannot process good fortune - too unexpected.

well-done.effect: Two words she's waited lifetime to hear.

for-once.quote: For once, he was proud of me
for-once.effect: Lifetime of rejection makes this moment precious.

given-face.effect: Her achievement raises his status - finally useful.

whole-being.quote: My whole being vibrated with all the joy in the world
whole-being.what: Joy as vibration through entire body.
whole-being.effect: Overwhelming physical response to emotional moment.

stretch-stars.quote: I only had to stretch out my hand to reach the stars
stretch-stars.effect: Impossible becomes possible in this moment.

only-one.quote: Perhaps I was the only one determined enough to enter and there were no other competitors!
only-one.what: Minimises achievement to avoid seeming proud.

doubt-it.quote: I doubt it very much but that's a good answer
doubt-it.effect: Modesty is proper behaviour for Chinese daughter.

now-never.effect: Must seize moment while father is pleased.

may-i-go.quote: May I go to university in England too, just like my brothers?
may-i-go.what: Asks for same opportunity as male siblings.
may-i-go.effect: Reveals gender discrimination - brothers automatically go.

have-potential.quote: I do believe you have potential
have-potential.effect: Potential not achievement - still qualified praise.

heart-lurch.quote: My heart gave a giant lurch
heart-lurch.effect: Joy so intense it's physically felt.

how-marvellous.quote: How marvellous it was simply to be alive!

entering-heaven.quote: Going to England is like entering heaven. Does it matter what you do after you get to heaven?
entering-heaven.effect: Escape from Hong Kong hell is everything.

writer-scoffed.quote: Writer!' he scoffed. 'You are going to starve!

rather-elementary.quote: your Chinese is actually rather elementary
rather-elementary.what: Denies her competence in own language.

waited-silence.quote: I waited in silence. I did not wish to contradict him
waited-silence.what: Knows not to argue when dreams crushed.
waited-silence.effect: Years of training - accept father's decisions.

medical-school.quote: you will go to medical school
medical-school.effect: Her achievement gives her education but not choice.

foolproof-profession.quote: That's a foolproof profession for you. Don't you agree?
foolproof-profession.effect: Illusion of consultation but decision made.

agree-course.effect: Shows she understands the game - agree or lose everything.

apparently-planned.quote: Apparently, he had it all planned out
apparently-planned.effect: Her achievement just triggered existing plan.

bliss-dawn.quote: Bliss was it in that dawn to be alive
bliss-dawn.what: References Romantic poem about French Revolution.
bliss-dawn.effect: Shows education despite father's dismissal - proves she's literary.

father-shall.quote: Father, I shall go to medical school in England and become a doctor. Thank you very, very much
father-shall.effect: Takes what she can get - half a dream better than none.

obstetrics.meaning: Medical field dealing with pregnancy and childbirth
obstetrics.note: Branch of medicine concerned with childbirth and care of women giving birth.
obstetrics.effect: Father chooses 'female-appropriate' medical field - even in medicine, gender limits her.

overview.heading: Why Mah Wrote This
overview.intro: Mah's purposes evolve through the passage:

points.label: To show childhood neglect
points.text: "I had forgotten" - Shows how excluded she was from family

points.label: To explore cultural values
points.text: "I had given him face" - Importance of status in Chinese culture

points.label: To show female limitation
points.text: "That's a foolproof profession for you" - Gender expectations

points.label: Western readers unfamiliar with Chinese culture
points.text: Explains concepts like "face", provides Hong Kong context

points.label: Those who experienced family rejection
points.text: Universal emotions of seeking parental approval

points.label: Young women facing limitations
points.text: Shows compromise between ambition and restriction

points.label: Fearful child
points.text: "Full of foreboding" - Constant anxiety about punishment

points.label: Disbelieving winner
points.text: "Is it possible? Am I dreaming?" - Cannot believe success

points.label: Ecstatic daughter
points.text: "My heart gave a giant lurch" - Physical joy

points.label: Physical metaphors
points.text: "throbbed... like a persistent toothache" - Makes anxiety physical

points.label: Celestial metaphor
points.text: "stretch out my hand to reach the stars" - Dreams within reach

points.label: Literary allusion
points.text: "Bliss was it in that dawn" - Wordsworth reference

overview.heading: How It's Organised
overview.intro: The passage's structure builds dramatic tension:

points.label: Fear to triumph
points.text: Opens with dread, peaks with achievement

points.label: Pivotal moment
points.text: "For once, he was proud of me" - Everything changes

points.label: Dream crushed and rebuilt
points.text: Writing dream denied, medical career imposed

points.label: Pragmatic resolution
points.text: "Thank you very, very much" - Accepts compromise gratefully
